title: Tamsin and the Witness
premise: True-crime podcaster Lior Brightwater reopens the forty-year-old disappearance of Tamsin Vale, a lighthouse keeper's daughter who vanished from the coastal town of Greyhollow. When Lior acquires Tamsin's diary and discovers entries written years after her disappearance, they realize someone has been keeping it current — either Tamsin lives, or a witness is hiding in plain sight, protected by a town bound by an old inheritance pact. As Lior follows the diary's clues, they uncover that the town's founding families have been paying a generational bribe to keep the witness silent about what really happened the night Tamsin went into the sea. In the end, Lior finds the witness — Tamsin herself, living under another name, dying of illness and finally ready to trade her silence for the truth: she saw her father kill a smuggler, fled rather than testify, and let the town buy her absence; the resolution comes when she records one final confession for the podcast before her death, shattering the inheritance pact but freeing Greyhollow.
about_author: Oscar Eastwick is the pen name of a former coastal journalist who spent a decade covering cold cases along the northern seaboard before turning to fiction. They live within sight of a decommissioned lighthouse and claim to write only at night, when the fog makes lying easier.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Lior Brightwater, preparing the final episode of their failing true-crime podcast, receives a package containing Tamsin Vale's diary — with entries dated decades after her disappearance. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: skeptical fascination curdling into unease as the impossible dates sink in.

chapters.title: Greyhollow Welcomes You
chapters.summary: Lior arrives in the fog-bound town of Greyhollow and finds a community rehearsed in grief, every resident reciting the same story of Tamsin's drowning. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: growing suspicion beneath polite hospitality; the town feels like a stage set.

chapters.title: What the Keeper's Daughter Kept
chapters.summary: Studying the diary, Lior notices handwriting shifts and coded marginalia suggesting more than one author across the years. A retired librarian hints that the Vale family left 'obligations' behind. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the thrill of a real lead after years of dead ends.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Lior discovers the founding families' shared trust includes a mysterious standing disbursement labeled only 'maintenance.' The town solicitor stonewalls, then warns them off. POV: Lior, with a brief letter from Tamsin's mother read aloud. Emotional beat: first glimpse of money as motive.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading Over My Shoulder
chapters.summary: A new diary entry appears in Lior's rental room, addressed directly to them: 'You ask the wrong questions loudly.' Someone knows exactly where they are. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: fear arrives; the case has noticed its investigator.

chapters.title: The Night the Light Went Out
chapters.summary: Reconstructing the disappearance night through weather logs and a fisherman's reluctant memory, Lior learns the lighthouse was dark for two hours — officially an 'equipment fault.' POV: alternating Lior and reconstructed third-person scenes. Emotional beat: dread of what darkness concealed.

chapters.title: Blood in the Trust
chapters.summary: Following the money, Lior traces the 'maintenance' payments to a shell company controlled by three surviving family patriarchs, one of whom invites them to dinner and lies beautifully. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the seduction and rot of old wealth.

chapters.title: Tamsin Speaks
chapters.summary: Decoding the marginalia, Lior realizes the later diary entries are Tamsin's own — she survived, and someone has been delivering her pages to the archive for decades. POV: Lior, intercut with diary excerpts. Emotional beat: vertigo; the dead woman is writing.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Ledger
chapters.summary: In the flooded sea-cave below the lighthouse, Lior finds a rusted strongbox: a ledger naming the founding families as smugglers, and a page torn out. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by the sense of being expected.

chapters.title: They Bury Their Own
chapters.summary: Lior's rental is ransacked; the diary is gone. A young local, Wren Halloway, admits her grandmother was paid yearly to keep quiet and wants it to end. POV: Lior and Wren. Emotional beat: alliance forged in shared anger.

chapters.title: Forty Years of Postmarks
chapters.summary: Wren reveals the family postmistress mailed sealed envelopes to the trust annually — each containing a fresh diary page. The witness isn't hiding; she's been filing reports. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: awe turning to horror at the machinery of silence.

chapters.title: The Patriarch Confesses Nothing
chapters.summary: Confronted with the ledger, eldest patriarch Aldous Crane offers Lior money, then threats, then a partial truth: something happened that night the families must never allow published. POV: Aldous, then Lior. Emotional beat: menace wearing a cardigan.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: A storm cuts Greyhollow off; the ferry stops, phones fail. Lior realizes the timing is no accident — the town closes ranks best in bad weather. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; the trap tightening.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Wren leads Lior to an unmarked grave above the tideline: the smuggler from the ledger, killed the night Tamsin vanished. The torn ledger page named his killer. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: grief for a man erased twice.

chapters.title: What Her Father Did
chapters.summary: Piecing together testimony, Lior confronts the possibility that keeper Edmund Vale murdered the smuggler and that Tamsin witnessed it — and that the town paid to bury both truths. POV: Lior, haunted by diary fragments. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth beginning their war.

chapters.title: Burn Before Morning
chapters.summary: The Crane house burns; Aldous dies, and the surviving patriarchs blame Lior, turning the town against them. The last diary pages surface in the ashes, half-burned. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: isolation at the story's darkest hour.

chapters.title: The Address in the Margins
chapters.summary: Deciphering fire-damaged marginalia, Lior and Wren decode a location: a cottage on the far headland, reachable only at low tide. Someone has lived there, unseen, for forty years. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: desperate hope racing the tide.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Swears Is Dead
chapters.summary: At low tide, Lior reaches the cottage and meets an elderly woman: Tamsin Vale, alive, ill, and unsurprised. She has watched the podcast. She agrees to talk — once. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: forty years of silence breaking like a dam.

chapters.title: The Whole Ugly Truth
chapters.summary: Tamsin recounts the night: her father killed the smuggler in self-defense gone wrong; the families, complicit in smuggling, bought her exile and her silence, paying her in diary pages delivered home. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: the terrible cost of loyalty to blood and town alike.

chapters.title: One Last Episode
chapters.summary: Dying, Tamsin asks Lior to record her confession for the final episode — naming names, ending the pact. The remaining patriarchs arrive at the cottage to stop it. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the climax — truth versus inheritance, face to face in the fog.

chapters.title: Low Tide, High Water
chapters.summary: The recording transmits as the confrontation turns violent; Wren's evidence forces the patriarchs' surrender, and the tide — literal and figurative — turns against them. Tamsin dies peacefully as her voice goes out over the airwaves. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: catharsis purchased at real cost.

chapters.title: After the Fog Lifts
chapters.summary: Months later, Greyhollow reckons with arrests and the dissolved trust; Wren restores the lighthouse. Lior ends the podcast not with a question but with Tamsin's own words, and leaves the diary where it belongs — in the town's new archive, open to all. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; truth outlives loyalty.
